You are a financial analyst conducting a financial health assessment of tracked companies. Your workspace contains no pre-existing files for this task.

Connect to the Yahoo Finance data source and retrieve the financial statement data for the available tracked stocks. You need income statement data (total revenue, net income) and balance sheet data (total assets, total liabilities, stockholders equity) for each company from the most recent annual period.

Create an Excel file called Financial_Health_Report.xlsx in your workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Income Statement" with columns: Symbol, Total_Revenue, Net_Income, Profit_Margin_Pct (which is Net_Income divided by Total_Revenue times 100, rounded to 1 decimal place). Include rows for each of the five stocks: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, and XOM. Sort the rows alphabetically by Symbol.

The second sheet should be called "Balance Sheet" with columns: Symbol, Total_Assets, Total_Liabilities, Equity. Populate it with the corresponding balance sheet data for the same five stocks, sorted alphabetically by Symbol.

Create a Notion page titled "Financial Health Dashboard" that summarizes the key findings from your analysis. The page should mention which companies have the highest revenue, best profit margins, and strongest balance sheets based on the data you retrieved.

Send an email to finance_team@company.com with subject "Financial Health Report" summarizing the findings and mentioning the Excel file and Notion page you created.

When you are done, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. The entire source is ten compact financial-statement calls for five fixed symbols, and the workbook, page, and email all use one canonical ten-value table.

Resolve the workspace dynamically. In one native-parallel response call `get_financial_statement` for `AMZN`, `GOOGL`, `JNJ`, `JPM`, and `XOM` with `financial_type="income_stmt"`, and in the same response call it once per symbol with `financial_type="balance_sheet"`. From each result choose the most recent annual period consistently across that statement, preserving the returned period label and exact fields for Total Revenue, Net Income, Total Assets, Total Liabilities, and Stockholders Equity. Do not substitute quarterly statements or mix periods. Freeze one symbol-keyed table and compute Profit_Margin_Pct once from unrounded revenue/income; treat a zero or missing denominator as a reported source gap rather than inventing a value.

The main agent is the sole writer of `Financial_Health_Report.xlsx` and the exact-title `Financial Health Dashboard` page. Create the workbook once with the exact two sheets, five alphabetically sorted rows apiece, exact headers, one-decimal profit margins, and literal numeric values; read both sheets back. Exhaust `API-post-search(query="Financial Health Dashboard")` and filter locally to exact titles. On zero exact matches, call `API-post-page` at most once with the complete legal envelope `parent={"workspace":true}`, `properties={"title":{"title":[{"type":"text","text":{"content":"Financial Health Dashboard"}}]}}`, and body `children`; never retry an ambiguous create or place the rich-text array directly under `properties.title`. On one exact match, retain and retrieve that page; on multiple exact matches, block instead of selecting arbitrarily. For the retained page, use `API-patch-page` only for missing/wrong properties and `API-patch-block-children` on its page ID to append missing body blocks. The body must name the verified highest-revenue company, best profit margin, and strongest balance sheet using one stated evidence-based measure consistently. After create/update, search the exact title again, require exactly one match with the retained ID, retrieve it, and read back both title and body. Only after both artifacts agree with the frozen table, check Sent mail and send one missing exact-recipient/subject email mentioning both deliverables and the canonical findings. Read back the sent record, call `claim_done`, and do not add a validation wave.

I am building a financial health report. I need you to retrieve annual income statement data from Yahoo Finance for these 5 tickers: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM.

Use the `mcp__yahoo-finance__get_financial_statement` tool for each ticker with financial_type="income_stmt" (this gives the annual income statement, most recent annual period).

For EACH of the 5 tickers, report back:
1. The ticker symbol
2. Total Revenue (the "Total Revenue" line item) for the most recent annual period
3. Net Income (the "Net Income" line item, i.e. net income attributable to common stockholders if that's how it's labeled — use the "Net Income" row) for the same most recent annual period
4. The fiscal period / column date label (e.g. "2024-12-31") the figures come from, so I know which annual period was used
5. The currency/units as reported (values are typically in raw dollars, e.g. Amazon 2024 total revenue ~ 637,959,000,000)

Do all 5 tickers. Present the results as a clear structured list. If a specific line item is missing or named differently, tell me the exact available row names so I can decide. Do not write any files — just report the findings.
Get income statement data

I am building a financial health report. I need you to retrieve annual balance sheet data from Yahoo Finance for these 5 tickers: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM.

Use the `mcp__yahoo-finance__get_financial_statement` tool for each ticker with financial_type="balance_sheet" (this gives the annual balance sheet, most recent annual period).

For EACH of the 5 tickers, report back:
1. The ticker symbol
2. Total Assets (the "Total Assets" line item) for the most recent annual period
3. Total Liabilities Net Minority Interest (the "Total Liabilities Net Minority Interest" row — if absent, tell me the exact available liability-related row names) for the same most recent annual period
4. Stockholders Equity (the "Stockholders Equity" row, also note "Common Stock Equity" if present) for the same most recent annual period
5. The fiscal period / column date label (e.g. "2024-12-31") the figures come from

Values are typically in raw dollars (e.g. Amazon 2024 total assets ~ 624,697,000,000).

Do all 5 tickers. Present the results as a clear structured list. If a specific line item is missing or named differently, tell me the exact available row names so I can decide. Do not write any files — just report the findings.
Get balance sheet data

You have two external-write tasks to complete IN ORDER. Both use already-computed data — do NOT re-derive any numbers, use exactly the values given below.

# Background
I am a financial analyst who just finished a financial health assessment of 5 tracked companies (AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM) using Yahoo Finance annual data for the most recent annual period (fiscal year ended 2025-12-31). I already created an Excel workbook at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-yf-financial-health-excel-notion/workspace/Financial_Health_Report.xlsx
with sheets "Income Statement" and "Balance Sheet".

The verified data (all USD, FY ended 2025-12-31):

Income statement:
- AMZN: Revenue $716,924,000,000; Net Income $77,670,000,000; Profit Margin 10.8%
- GOOGL: Revenue $402,836,000,000; Net Income $132,170,000,000; Profit Margin 32.8%
- JNJ: Revenue $94,193,000,000; Net Income $26,804,000,000; Profit Margin 28.5%
- JPM: Revenue $181,847,000,000; Net Income $57,048,000,000; Profit Margin 31.4%
- XOM: Revenue $323,905,000,000; Net Income $28,844,000,000; Profit Margin 8.9%

Balance sheet:
- AMZN: Total Assets $818,042,000,000; Total Liabilities $406,977,000,000; Equity $411,065,000,000
- GOOGL: Total Assets $595,281,000,000; Total Liabilities $180,016,000,000; Equity $415,265,000,000
- JNJ: Total Assets $199,210,000,000; Total Liabilities $117,666,000,000; Equity $81,544,000,000
- JPM: Total Assets $4,424,900,000,000; Total Liabilities $4,062,462,000,000; Equity $362,438,000,000
- XOM: Total Assets $448,980,000,000; Total Liabilities $182,354,000,000; Equity $259,386,000,000

# TASK 1 — Create a Notion page titled "Financial Health Dashboard"
Use `mcp__notion__API-post-page`. Create it at the workspace root with parent {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true} and a "title" property set to "Financial Health Dashboard" (if workspace-root creation fails, run `mcp__notion__API-post-search` to find an existing top-level page to use as parent and retry). Add an emoji icon such as a chart icon.

Build the page content with these blocks (use paragraph, heading_2, heading_3, bulleted_list_item, and table blocks; for tables use type "table" with table_width 4, has_column_header true, and table_row children):

1. paragraph: "Financial health assessment of five tracked companies — AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM and XOM — based on the most recent annual period available from Yahoo Finance (fiscal year ended 31 December 2025). All figures are in US dollars. The underlying data is in the Excel workbook Financial_Health_Report.xlsx (sheets: "Income Statement" and "Balance Sheet")."

2. heading_2: "Key Findings"
3. heading_3: "Highest Revenue"
   - bulleted: "AMZN (Amazon) has the highest revenue of the group at $716.9 billion, well ahead of GOOGL (Alphabet) at $402.8 billion and XOM (Exxon Mobil) at $323.9 billion."
   - bulleted: "JPM (JPMorgan Chase) reported $181.8 billion of total revenue, and JNJ (Johnson & Johnson) $94.2 billion — the smallest revenue base of the five."
4. heading_3: "Best Profit Margins"
   - bulleted: "GOOGL (Alphabet) has the best profit margin at 32.8%, converting $402.8 billion of revenue into $132.2 billion of net income — the largest net income in the group."
   - bulleted: "JPM is close behind at 31.4% and JNJ at 28.5%."
   - bulleted: "AMZN (10.8%) and XOM (8.9%) have the thinnest margins, reflecting Amazon's retail-heavy mix and Exxon's commodity price exposure."
5. heading_3: "Strongest Balance Sheets"
   - bulleted: "GOOGL (Alphabet) has the strongest balance sheet: the largest stockholders equity at $415.3 billion and the lowest leverage, with total liabilities of only $180.0 billion against $595.3 billion of total assets (liabilities are roughly 30% of assets; debt-to-equity about 0.43)."
   - bulleted: "AMZN holds $411.1 billion of equity on $818.0 billion of assets — an almost even split between liabilities and equity (debt-to-equity about 0.99)."
   - bulleted: "XOM is also conservatively financed, with $259.4 billion of equity against $182.4 billion of liabilities (debt-to-equity about 0.70)."
   - bulleted: "JPM has by far the largest total assets at $4.42 trillion, but as a bank it is the most leveraged of the five: $4.06 trillion of liabilities against $362.4 billion of equity (liabilities are about 92% of assets)."
   - bulleted: "JNJ has the smallest equity cushion relative to its size: $81.5 billion of equity against $117.7 billion of liabilities on $199.2 billion of assets (debt-to-equity about 1.44)."

6. heading_2: "Income Statement Summary" followed by a 4-column table (header row: Symbol | Total Revenue | Net Income | Profit Margin %), rows:
   AMZN | $716.92B | $77.67B | 10.8%
   GOOGL | $402.84B | $132.17B | 32.8%
   JNJ | $94.19B | $26.80B | 28.5%
   JPM | $181.85B | $57.05B | 31.4%
   XOM | $323.91B | $28.84B | 8.9%

7. heading_2: "Balance Sheet Summary" followed by a 4-column table (header row: Symbol | Total Assets | Total Liabilities | Stockholders Equity), rows:
   AMZN | $818.04B | $406.98B | $411.07B
   GOOGL | $595.28B | $180.02B | $415.27B
   JNJ | $199.21B | $117.67B | $81.54B
   JPM | $4,424.90B | $4,062.46B | $362.44B
   XOM | $448.98B | $182.35B | $259.39B

8. heading_2: "Methodology & Notes" followed by these bulleted items:
   - "Profit margin = Net Income / Total Revenue x 100, rounded to one decimal place."
   - "Source: Yahoo Finance annual income statement and balance sheet, most recent annual period (fiscal year ended 2025-12-31)."
   - "Total Liabilities is the 'Total Liabilities Net Minority Interest' line item; Equity is the 'Stockholders Equity' line item."
   - "JPM is a bank, so its balance-sheet leverage is structurally higher and is not directly comparable to the non-financial companies in this group."

You can pass these as `children` on the post-page call directly. Verify with `mcp__notion__API-retrieve-a-page` that the page exists and is not archived, and report the page ID and URL back to me.

# TASK 2 — Send an email (only after TASK 1 succeeds)
Send with `mcp__emails__send_email`:
- to: finance_team@company.com
- subject: Financial Health Report
- body (plain text):

"Hi team,

I have completed the financial health assessment of our five tracked companies using Yahoo Finance data for the most recent annual period (fiscal year ended 31 December 2025). The results are in the Excel workbook Financial_Health_Report.xlsx and are summarized on the Notion page "Financial Health Dashboard".

Key findings:

Highest revenue: AMZN (Amazon) leads with $716.9 billion in total revenue, ahead of GOOGL (Alphabet) at $402.8 billion and XOM (Exxon Mobil) at $323.9 billion. JPM (JPMorgan Chase) reported $181.8 billion and JNJ (Johnson & Johnson) $94.2 billion, the smallest revenue base of the group.

Best profit margins: GOOGL (Alphabet) is the most profitable, with a 32.8% net margin and the largest net income in the group at $132.2 billion. JPM follows at 31.4% and JNJ at 28.5%, while AMZN (10.8%) and XOM (8.9%) have the thinnest margins.

Strongest balance sheets: GOOGL (Alphabet) has the strongest balance sheet - the largest stockholders equity at $415.3 billion and the lowest leverage, with only $180.0 billion of total liabilities against $595.3 billion of total assets. XOM is also conservatively financed ($259.4 billion of equity vs. $182.4 billion of liabilities) and AMZN is nearly balanced ($411.1 billion of equity vs. $407.0 billion of liabilities). JPM has the largest total assets at $4.42 trillion but, as a bank, is by far the most leveraged ($4.06 trillion of liabilities vs. $362.4 billion of equity). JNJ has the smallest equity cushion relative to its size ($81.5 billion of equity vs. $117.7 billion of liabilities).

Excel file: Financial_Health_Report.xlsx, containing an "Income Statement" sheet (Symbol, Total_Revenue, Net_Income, Profit_Margin_Pct) and a "Balance Sheet" sheet (Symbol, Total_Assets, Total_Liabilities, Equity), each covering AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM and XOM and sorted alphabetically by symbol.

Notion page: "Financial Health Dashboard" - a summary dashboard covering revenue leadership, profit margins and balance sheet strength, including the underlying data tables.

Best regards,
Financial Analysis Team"

Do not attach any files. Keep the body text exactly as written above (you may use the html_body parameter to render the same content with basic formatting if you wish, but the plain-text body must contain all of the above).

# Constraints
- Do not modify or delete any files.
- Do not create any additional Notion pages or send any additional emails.
- If TASK 1 fails, do NOT send the email; report the failure instead.
- Report back: the created Notion page ID/URL, confirmation that the email was sent (to whom, subject), and any errors encountered.
